## Load libraries and data

```{r}
library("tidyverse")

cancer_data_augmented <- read_csv(file = "../data/03_cancer_data_augmented.csv",
                                  show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  mutate(age_group = factor(age_group, levels = c("<65", "65-74", ">=75")))

```

### Age Group Analyses

```{R}
without_NA <- cancer_data_augmented %>% drop_na(age_group)
```

```{r}
# Blood pressure over age group 
ggplot(data = without_NA,
       mapping = aes(x = age_group,
                     y = mean_arterial_pressure)) +
  geom_boxplot()
```

```{R}
# Prostatic acid phosphatase over age group
  ggplot(data = without_NA,
       mapping = aes(x = age_group,
                     y = prostatic_acid_phosphatase)) +
  geom_boxplot() + scale_y_continuous(trans='log10')
```

```{R}
# This plot shows the heart disease history over age. It shows more as age groups are not equal in size.
ggplot(without_NA, aes(age, heart_disease_history)) +
  geom_jitter(height = 0.03, alpha = 0.3) +
  geom_smooth(method = "glm", method.args = list(family = binomial)) +
  labs(y = "Heart disease history")
```

```{R}
# Age groups are of different sizes. Look at the relative distribution 
  ggplot(data = without_NA,
       mapping = aes(x = age_group,
                     y = baseline_electrocardiogram)) +
  geom_count()
```

```{R}
# Hemoglobin levels in serum over age groups. Shows us that there is no real correlation.
  ggplot(data = without_NA,
       mapping = aes(x = age_group,
                     y = serum_hemoglobin)) +
  geom_boxplot()
```

```{R}
  ggplot(data = without_NA,
       mapping = aes(x = age,
                     y = age_group)) +
  geom_col()
```

```{R}
# Here I want to plot if there is a correlation between cancer stage and age at death. 
  ggplot(data = without_NA,
       mapping = aes(x = age_group,
                     y = death_cause)) +
  geom_count()
```


```{R}
#| fig-width: 10
ggplot(data = without_NA, mapping=aes(x=estrogen_treatment, y=follow_up_months, fill = age_group))+
  geom_boxplot() + facet_wrap(vars(age_group))

# Here, follow up months over estrogen treatment is mapped for each age group. It is interesting to see that the differences between the placebo and 0.2 mg, as for people under 65 the effect seems reversed.
```
```{R}
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 4
ggplot(data = without_NA, mapping=aes(x=estrogen_treatment, y=heart_disease_history, fill = age_group))+
  geom_col() +facet_wrap(vars(age_group))

# Here, estrogen treatment is compared to heart disease history for each age group.
```

```{R}
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 4
ggplot(data = without_NA, mapping=aes(x=estrogen_treatment, y=prostatic_acid_phosphatase, fill = age_group))+
  geom_boxplot() +facet_wrap(vars(age_group)) +scale_y_continuous(trans='log10')

# Here, estrogen treatment is compared to prostatic acid phosphatase, within each age group. Unfortunately it does not show a clear correlation.
```

```{R}
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 4
ggplot(data = without_NA, mapping=aes(x=estrogen_treatment, y=mean_arterial_pressure, fill = age_group))+
  geom_boxplot() +facet_wrap(vars(age_group)) +scale_y_continuous(trans='log10')
# mean arterial pressure over estrogen treatment. Again, no clear correlation. 
```
```{R}
ggplot(data=without_NA, mapping=aes(x=estrogen_treatment, y=vital_status, colour=age_group)) +
  geom_count() + facet_wrap(vars(age_group))
# in all groups, 1 mg estrogen seems to have a positive effect on the vital status of the patients
```
